source_text: ea locutione dictum esse: In quo omnes peccaverunt, ac si diceretur: Propter quod omnes peccaverunt; sicut dictum est: In quo corrigit iunior viam suam ; ut scilicet non in uno homine omnes homines peccasse intellegantur originaliter, et tamquam in massae unione communiter; sed propterea quia primus hominum ille peccavit; id est, cum imitantur illum, non cum generantur ex illo. Non ergo huic sensui convenit illa locutio, ita dictum esse: in quo, velut dictum esset
pass_a_gloss: She/it locutione dictum to-be: in whither all peccaverunt, and if to-say: because-of that/which all peccaverunt; as dictum is: in whither corrigit iunior viam his-own; so-that/as namely not in uno homine all human-beings peccasse intellegantur originaliter, and tamquam in of-the-mass unione in-common; but propterea because first of-human-beings that peccavit; it is, when/with imitantur that, not when/with generantur from illo. not therefore to-this sensui convenit that locutio, so dictum to-be: in whither, as-if dictum would-be.
pass_b_english: The expression ‘in whom all sinned’ is used as though it said ‘because of which all sinned,’ just as it says, ‘By what does a young man correct his way?’ (Romans 5:12; Psalm 119:9, LXX/Vulgate Psalm 118:9)

Augustine reports Julian’s interpretation: all people are not to be understood as having sinned originally in one man, together as though united in a single mass. Rather, they sin because the first man sinned—by imitating him, not by being born from him.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
